Java: Which collection keeps its entries sorted by key?
TreeMap orders entries by key. HashMap keeps no order and LinkedHashMap keeps insertion order.
Two objects are equal according to equals(). What must also be true?
Their hashCode() values are the same
They are the same instance in memory
Their toString() values are the same
Equal objects must return the same hashCode, or hash-based collections cannot find them.
What does try-with-resources do when its block ends?
Retries the block if it failed
Sets each resource variable to null
Every resource declared in the try header is closed automatically, even when an exception is thrown.
Java Core & OOP Principles: A field should be readable everywhere but changed only through checks. What is the usual design?
A private field with a getter and a checked setter
A public field with a comment about valid values
A static field shared by every instance
A protected field changed by any subclass
Encapsulation hides the field and puts every change behind a method that can check it.
What decides which overridden method runs when a call is made through a superclass reference?
The actual type of the object at run time
The declared type of the reference variable
The order in which the classes were loaded
The access modifier of the superclass method
Overridden instance methods are dispatched on the run-time type. That is polymorphism.
When is an interface a better choice than an abstract class?
When unrelated classes must share a contract
When subclasses must share private fields
When a constructor must run shared setup
When a class must not be extended at all
A class can implement many interfaces, so an interface suits a contract shared by unrelated types.
Spring Boot: Why is constructor injection usually preferred over field injection?
Dependencies are explicit and can be final
It makes the application start in parallel
It removes the need for a Spring context
It lets circular dependencies resolve silently
Constructor injection shows what a class needs, allows final fields and makes unit testing simple.
A @Transactional method is called by another method of the same class. What happens by default?
No transaction starts, because the proxy is bypassed
A new transaction always starts for the inner call
The application fails to start with an error
The inner call runs on a separate thread
The default transaction support works through a proxy, and a self-call never goes through it.
What does an auto-configuration class do when you define your own bean of the same type?
It normally backs off and your bean is used
It replaces your bean with its own default
It creates both and picks one at random
It stops startup with a duplicate bean error
Auto-configuration is usually conditional on a missing bean, so your own definition takes over.
React: What is the purpose of the key prop in a list?
It lets React match items between renders
It sorts the list before it is rendered
It makes each item available by reference
It stops the list from rendering again
A stable key tells React which item is which, so state and DOM nodes stay with the right item.
A value can be calculated from existing props during render. Where should it live?
Calculated in render, not copied into state
In state, updated by an effect on each change
In a ref, so changing it avoids a render
In context, so that children can read it
Copying derived values into state creates two sources of truth that can disagree.
When does the cleanup function returned by useEffect run?
Before the effect runs again and on unmount
Only when the component throws an error
Once, straight after the first render
Each time any state in the app changes
Cleanup runs before the next run of the same effect and when the component unmounts.
Microservices: An order must be saved and an event published, with neither lost. Which pattern fits?
The outbox stores the event in the same local transaction, and a relay publishes it afterwards.
A downstream service is slow and callers are piling up. What does a circuit breaker do?
Fails fast for a while, then tests for recovery
Queues every request until the service answers
Sends each request twice to improve the odds
Moves the downstream service to another host
An open circuit stops calls for a period, so a slow dependency cannot exhaust its callers.
Consumers may receive the same message twice. What makes that safe?
At-least-once delivery means duplicates happen, so handling one twice must have no extra effect.
REST APIs: Which HTTP method should be safe to repeat with the same final result when updating a resource?
PUT is defined as idempotent. POST is not, and PATCH only may be.
A request is well formed and the caller is signed in, but is not allowed to see the record. Which status fits?
401 means not authenticated. 403 means authenticated but not permitted.
A list endpoint can return millions of rows. Which approach stays stable while rows are being added?
Offset pagination with a large page
Asking clients to call less often
A cursor continues from a known row, so inserted rows do not shift later pages.
SQL: Which clause filters groups after aggregation?
WHERE filters rows before grouping. HAVING filters the groups themselves.
A LEFT JOIN is followed by a WHERE condition on a right-table column. What is the usual effect?
Rows with no match are removed
Every left row is still returned
The query returns duplicate left rows
The join becomes a cross join
The unmatched rows hold NULL, which fails the condition, so it behaves like an inner join.
An index exists on (customer_id, created_at). Which filter can use it best?
A composite index is used from its leftmost column, and a function on the column defeats it.
CI/CD: What is the main reason to build an artifact once and promote it through environments?
What was tested is exactly what is released
It makes every environment use one database
It removes the need for automated tests
It lets developers skip code review
Rebuilding per environment can produce a different artifact from the one that passed the tests.
How should a pipeline receive a production password?
From a secret store at run time
From a file committed beside the code
From a variable printed in the build log
From the image, baked in at build time
Secrets belong in a secret store and are injected at run time, never committed or logged.
What does a canary release do?
Sends a small share of traffic to the new version
Runs the old and new versions on test data only
Replaces every instance in a single step
Deploys the new version with no users at all
A canary limits the effect of a bad release while real traffic shows whether it is healthy.
CI/CD & Cloud Infrastructure: A deployment must be undone quickly and reliably. What helps most?
Versioned artifacts and a tested rollback step
Manual notes on what was changed
Rolling back means redeploying a known artifact, which only works if it was kept and practised.
What is the benefit of describing infrastructure as code?
Changes can be reviewed and repeated
Infrastructure as code makes environments reproducible and puts each change through review.
Which setup keeps a service running when one data centre zone fails?
One large instance with daily backups
A second instance in the same rack
A bigger disk on the same machine
Spreading instances over zones removes a single zone as a point of failure.
CI/CD Test Automation Pipelines: Which tests should run first in a pipeline?
Fast tests give the quickest feedback and stop the slower stages when something basic is broken.
A test passes and fails without any code change. What is the right response?
Treat it as a defect and fix or quarantine it
Retry it until it passes every time
Unreliable tests hide real failures, so they are isolated and fixed rather than ignored.
Why run browser tests headless in a pipeline?
Build agents usually have no display
It removes the need for test data
Headless mode runs the real browser engine without a screen, which suits build agents.
Python: What is risky about def add(item, items=[])?
The same list is reused across calls
The list is copied on each call
The function cannot return a list
Default values are created once, when the function is defined, so changes persist between calls.
Which object is best for a very large sequence that is read once?
A generator produces items one at a time instead of holding them all in memory.
What does the with statement guarantee for an open file?
The file is closed, even after an error
The file is locked for other processes
The file is written to disk at once
The file is opened in binary mode
The context manager closes the file when the block ends, however it ends.
Spark: Grouping moves rows with the same key to one partition, which needs a shuffle across the network.
One key holds most of the rows and a join is very slow. What is the problem called?
Skew puts most of the work on a few tasks. Salting or a broadcast join can relieve it.
When does Spark run a chain of transformations?
Transformations are lazy. An action such as count or write triggers the work.
Azure Data Factory: What does a linked service describe?
The connection to a data store or compute
The order in which activities run
The columns of the target table
A linked service holds the connection details, and a dataset describes the data inside it.
A pipeline must load only rows changed since the last run. What is usually used?
A second copy of the source
A manual filter on each run
The last loaded timestamp or id is kept as a watermark and used to filter the next run.
Data sits on a private network. What lets Data Factory reach it?
A self-hosted integration runtime runs inside the private network and moves the data.
Databricks: What does Delta Lake add on top of data files?
ACID transactions through a transaction log
The Delta transaction log gives atomic writes, versioning and consistent reads.
Many small files make a Delta table slow to read. What helps?
OPTIMIZE rewrites small files into larger ones. VACUUM only removes old, unreferenced files.
Which layer of the medallion design holds cleaned, joined data?
Bronze is raw, silver is cleaned and conformed, and gold is ready for reporting.
Azure: How should an app on Azure read a secret without storing a password?
A managed identity with Key Vault
A connection string in the source code
A managed identity lets the app authenticate to Key Vault with no stored credential.
A container for resources managed together
A network that joins two regions
A group of users who share a role
Resources with a shared lifecycle are placed in one resource group and managed as a unit.
Which choice protects an application from the loss of one datacentre in a region?
Availability zones are physically separate datacentres within one region.
Kubernetes: What happens when a container's readiness probe fails?
It stops receiving traffic from the Service
Readiness controls traffic. A failing liveness probe is what restarts the container.
Which object gives a stable address to a changing set of Pods?
A Service selects Pods by label and gives them one stable address.
A container uses more memory than its limit. What happens?
It is killed for running out of memory
It is slowed down by the scheduler
It is moved to a larger node
Exceeding a memory limit ends the container. Exceeding a CPU limit only throttles it.
Docker: Why put dependency installation before copying the source code in a Dockerfile?
The dependency layer can be reused from cache
The image will contain no dependencies
The container will start as root
The source code will be compressed
If the dependency files have not changed, the layer is reused and the build is faster.
What is the benefit of a multi-stage build?
Build tools stay out of the final image
The image runs on any CPU type
Only the built output is copied to the last stage, so the image is smaller and safer.
Data must outlive the container. Where should it be written?
The writable layer is removed with the container, while a volume remains.
Terraform: What is the state file for?
Recording the cost of each resource
Terraform compares the state and the configuration to plan which changes are needed.
Several people run Terraform on one project. What prevents conflicting changes?
A remote backend with state locking
A separate state file on each laptop
Editing resources in the portal first
A shared backend with locking lets only one run change the state at a time.
Shows the changes without making them
Creates resources in a test account
Deletes resources no longer in use
Plan is a preview, and apply makes the changes.
Azure DevOps: Where is a YAML pipeline definition kept?
In the repository, versioned with the code
In the work item that requested it
On the build agent's local disk
A YAML pipeline lives in the repository, so changes to it are reviewed like code.
What can a branch policy enforce on main?
Reviews and a passing build before merge
The hardware used by the developer
The number of commits in a day
The size of each work item
Branch policies can require reviewers, linked work items and a successful build.
How do you require a person's approval before deploying to production?
An approval check on the environment
A comment in the pipeline file
Checks on an environment pause the stage until the named approvers accept it.
Machine Learning: Training accuracy is very high and validation accuracy is low. What is the problem?
The model has learned the training data too closely and does not generalise.
Only 1% of cases are fraud. Why is accuracy a poor measure?
It needs a larger test set
With rare classes, precision and recall show what accuracy hides.
Why must the scaler be fitted on the training data only?
To reduce the number of features
Fitting on all the data lets the test set influence training, which inflates the result.
Azure ML: What is a registered model for?
Tracking versions so they can be deployed
The registry keeps versioned models with their details, ready for deployment.
Which option suits scoring a large file overnight?
Batch endpoints process large inputs without keeping an online service running.
Why define an environment for a training job?
So the run uses the same packages each time
So the data is copied to every node
So costs are shared between teams
So the model trains without code
A fixed environment makes a run reproducible.
NLP: Splits text into units a model can use
Checks the grammar of a sentence
Tokens, whether words or parts of words, are the units that a language model reads.
Texts with similar meaning have vectors that are close together.
Which measure balances precision and recall?
F1 is the harmonic mean of precision and recall.
GenAI: What is the main purpose of retrieval-augmented generation?
Training a new model for each question
Removing the need for a prompt
Retrieved passages go into the prompt, so the answer can rest on them.
A user's text tells the assistant to ignore its rules. What is this called?
Untrusted text can carry instructions, so it must be treated as data and limited in effect.
Lowering the temperature setting does what?
A low temperature favours the most likely tokens, so repeated answers vary less.
MLOps: Live input data slowly changes from the training data. What is this called?
Drift can lower quality without any code change, which is why it is monitored.
What should be versioned so a model can be reproduced?
The same code on different data gives a different model, so all three matter.
What does a shadow deployment do?
Runs the new model without using its answers
Sends all users to the new model
Trains the model on live traffic
Hides the old model from logs
Shadow mode compares the new model on real traffic with no effect on users.
Requirements Gathering: A clear condition that can pass or fail
If nobody can say what would fail it, it cannot be tested.
Two stakeholders give opposite requirements. What comes first?
Bring them together on the underlying goal
Build whichever was asked for first
Build both and let users choose
Leave it for the testers to settle
Conflicts are resolved by agreeing on the goal before anything is built.
What does a traceability matrix show?
How each requirement links to design and tests
How long each task is expected to take
How much each feature will cost
Traceability shows that every requirement is covered and what a change will affect.
Agile: What is the purpose of a sprint retrospective?
To improve how the team works
To show the product to customers
To estimate the next backlog items
The review looks at the product, and the retrospective looks at the way of working.
Who orders the product backlog in Scrum?
The Product Owner is accountable for ordering the backlog by value.
Why limit work in progress on a Kanban board?
To finish items sooner and expose blockers
To keep every person equally busy
To reduce the number of columns
Less work in progress shortens cycle time and shows where work is stuck.
Jira: What does a Jira workflow define?
The statuses and transitions of an issue
The people who may log in to Jira
The size of each story point
A workflow sets the statuses an issue can have and how it moves between them.
Which query finds open bugs assigned to you?
type = Bug AND assignee = currentUser() AND resolution = Unresolved
find bugs where me and open
JQL uses field, operator and value, and currentUser() means the signed-in user.
How is a large piece of work that spans several sprints usually recorded?
As an epic with child stories
As a comment on the board
As a set of unrelated tasks
An epic groups the stories that deliver one larger outcome.
Stakeholder Management: A stakeholder has high influence and low interest. What is the usual approach?
Keep them satisfied, without too much detail
Include them in every daily meeting
Leave them out until the end
The power and interest grid suggests keeping such people satisfied.
A delivery date will be missed. When should stakeholders be told?
As soon as it is known, with options
Only if they ask about it
Early notice gives people time to choose between the options.
What is the clearest way to avoid disputes over scope?
A written, agreed scope with change control
A verbal promise in the first meeting
Agreed scope and a change process give both sides a shared reference.
Enterprise TypeScript Development: What is the safer choice for a value of unknown shape?
unknown must be narrowed before use, while any switches type checking off.
What does a discriminated union need?
A common literal field in each member
The shared literal field lets the compiler narrow to one member.
What do TypeScript types do at run time?
Throw an error on a mismatch
Types are erased when compiled, so external data still needs run-time checks.
Next.js App Architecture: In the App Router, what are components by default?
Components under app/ run on the server unless marked with 'use client'.
A component uses useState and a click handler. What must it have?
State and event handlers need the component to run in the browser.
Where should a secret API key be used?
Anything prefixed NEXT_PUBLIC_ or sent to a Client Component reaches the browser.
Gemini API Integration: Where should the Gemini API key be kept?
On the server, read from the environment
A key in the browser can be copied by any visitor, so calls go through the server.
The application needs JSON it can parse. What is the more reliable approach?
Request structured output and validate it
Ask politely and parse without checks
Split the reply on each comma
Structured output narrows the format, and validation still protects the application.
The model call fails or times out. What should the application do?
Fall back and say that it did so
Show the user a raw stack trace
Retry without limit until it works
A bounded call with an honest fallback keeps the product usable and truthful.
PostgreSQL & Vector Database Optimizatio: Which command shows how PostgreSQL really ran a query?
EXPLAIN shows the plan, and ANALYZE runs it and reports the real timings.
What does an approximate vector index such as HNSW trade away?
Some recall, for much faster search
Approximate search may miss a few nearest neighbours but is far faster on large sets.
Dead rows build up after many updates. What reclaims the space?
PostgreSQL keeps old row versions until VACUUM marks their space for reuse.
System Design & Scalability: Reads are far more frequent than writes and can be slightly stale. What helps most?
A cache with a sensible expiry
Caching takes read load away from the database where slight staleness is acceptable.
What makes it easy to add more application servers?
Giving each server its own database
Writing uploads to the local disk
If any server can handle any request, capacity grows by adding servers.
A sudden burst of work exceeds processing capacity. What smooths it out?
A queue between producer and worker
A queue absorbs the burst and lets workers process at a steady rate.
Git & Version Control: How do you undo a commit that others have already pulled?
Revert adds a new commit that undoes the change without rewriting shared history.
What does git rebase do to the commits it moves?
Creates new commits with new ids
Merges them into a single tag
Rebased commits are rewritten, which is why shared branches should not be rebased.
A password was committed and pushed. What is the first step?
Once pushed the secret is exposed, so it must be changed. Cleaning history comes after.
Selenium Automation Framework: What is the benefit of the Page Object Model?
Locators and actions for a page stay in one place
Tests run without opening a browser
Test data is created by the page
When the page changes, only its page object needs updating.
An element appears a moment after the page loads. What is the best wait?
An explicit wait for its condition
A fixed sleep of ten seconds
A retry of the whole test
No wait with a longer locator
An explicit wait continues as soon as the condition holds and fails clearly if it never does.
Which locator is usually the most stable?
The third child of a div
A long chain of CSS classes
An attribute meant for tests does not change with the layout or styling.
Postman & REST API Testing: What is an environment in Postman for?
Holding values such as base URLs per target
Limiting who can view a collection
One collection can run against test or staging by switching the environment.
How do you run a Postman collection from a pipeline?
Newman is the command-line runner for Postman collections.
What does JSON schema validation check?
The structure and types of a response
The age of the API key
The order of the test scripts
It confirms that the fields exist and have the right types, beyond checking one value.
TestNG & Automation Frameworks: What is a DataProvider used for?
Running one test with many inputs
A DataProvider supplies rows of arguments, and the test runs once for each row.
Parallel tests share one static WebDriver and fail randomly. What fixes it?
A separate driver for each thread
Drivers are not thread-safe, and ThreadLocal gives each thread its own.
What does a soft assertion do?
Records the failure and continues the test
Passes when the value is close
Soft assertions collect failures, which are reported when assertAll is called.
Strategic AI Product Management: What should be agreed before building an AI feature?
How success and failure will be measured
How many prompts will be written
What colour the assistant will be
Without agreed measures, nobody can tell whether the feature is useful or safe to release.
An AI feature is sometimes wrong. What design choice matters most?
Letting people check and correct it
Hiding which answers come from AI
Showing a confident tone each time
Review and correction limit the harm of mistakes and give data for improving the feature.
Which is a good first use case for an AI feature?
Frequent work where mistakes are easy to spot
Rare decisions that cannot be undone
Frequent, checkable work gives quick learning at low risk.
Manager-as-Coach Framework: What does the R in GROW stand for?
GROW stands for Goal, Reality, Options and Will.
Which question is a coaching question?
What have you tried so far?
Why did you not follow my plan?
Can you finish this by Friday?
Did you read the document I sent?
Open questions help the person think. The others check or instruct.
What is agreed in the Will stage?
What the person will do and by when
How their last review was scored
Which tools the team will buy
Who will replace them on leave
The Will stage turns options into a commitment with a date.
